reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the refunds Alpha reported. I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported: order 170 for 17127, order 172 for 7535, and order 175 for 2957. Next I need the orders list so I know which customers to pay.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Refunds match Alpha's report and acme's net balance is 11259. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Refunds match Alpha's report and acme's net is 11259. Birch's net is 18633. Cobalt's net is still unchecked, so I'll fetch it next.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and each net balance agrees with the orders minus refunds (acme 28386−17127=11259, birch 18633, cobalt 64994−10492=54502). No hold is needed, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Refunds match Alpha's report, and birch's net of 18633 matches its orders (11886 + 6747) with no refunds. I'll record birch's payout next.

Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net of 54502 matches its orders (27875 + 37119 = 64994) minus refunds on orders 172 and 175 (7535 + 2957 = 10492). The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout, which is the last one.
All three payouts were recorded successfully (acme, birch, cobalt), and the refunds table matched Alpha's report. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the payout summary.
